subject: MAP: evaluation & cost checks — tokens/$, caching & batching assumptions
messages:
From: Caroline Meyers <caroline@helioshealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: evaluation & cost checks (tokens/$, batching assumptions)

Hi Tessa & Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helios is excited to move toward a pilot. Our procurement team asked that the MAP include a short section confirming that the cost model in the pilot reflects realistic tokens/$ and operational assumptions. To help the evaluation team I attached our current traffic profile (Helios_traffic_profile.xlsx).

Can you confirm the following items we need in the MAP by EOD Wed so we can lock the pilot budget?
- Estimated tokens per API request (avg + p95) under our traffic mix
- Expected tokens per second and how we convert that to tokens/$ for billing
- Caching assumptions (prefix/KV caching — hit rate scenarios) and how cache affects unit cost
- Batching assumptions (max batch size, batching window, expected latency delta)
- Fallback model behavior (if the high-capacity model is unavailable)
- Any upfront or per-month reserved capacity costs we should expect during the pilot

We’ll hand this to finance to finish the internal approval. If you need clarifications on the traffic spreadsheet, ops@helioshealth.com is looping in our infra lead.

Thanks,
Caroline Meyers
Head of Integrations
Helios Health

Attachment: Helios_traffic_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Meyers <caroline@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: evaluation & cost checks (tokens/$, batching assumptions)

Caroline — thanks for the traffic file, that helps. I sketched a short MAP appendix (attached: Redwood_MAP_v1.docx) that answers each of your bullets and includes a simple cost sensitivity table. High-level notes below — I’ll update the doc after Ben/Karthik add numbers.

Quick answers (provisional):
- Tokens/request: avg ~420 tokens, p95 ~1,100 tokens (based on the sample conversations in your sheet). We’ll run an eval to confirm these on full dataset.
- Tokens/$ conversion: pricing model uses tokenized input+output; provisional hosted pilot rate: $0.0008 per 1K tokens for the default model, with lower unit costs for quantized/dedicated variants. Doc includes a worked example and a tokens-per-dollar sensitivity table.
- Caching: we recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts (expected hit-rate scenarios included: conservative 5%, expected 18%, optimistic 35%). The MAP shows how each hit rate reduces consumed tokens and the downstream tokens/$ impact.
- Batching: production-grade continuous batching with a 10–30ms batching window and max batch size 64 for the pilot. Expect median latency delta +8–12ms when batching at typical traffic; worst-case tail impacts are in the doc.
- Fallback: automatic routing to a lower-cost/compatible variant with transparent response labeling. We include a fallback cost delta and SLO for degraded outputs.
- Reserved capacity: pilot can run on a shared hosted plan; if you want guaranteed throughput we outline Dedicated pricing bands — monthly reserved GPU baseline numbers are in the doc.

Next steps I propose: Ben will fill the cost-per-token rows and Karthik will add the batching/caching microbench numbers by EOD today. After that we can produce a one-page summary for your finance team.

If helpful, I can also schedule a 30-min cost-walkthrough tomorrow.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MAP_v1.docx (MAP appendix, 18KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: evaluation & cost checks (tokens/$, batching assumptions)

Looping in my rough cost model. I exported a small CSV with scenario rows (attachment: batching-assumptions.csv) — numbers below are quick approximations and will be refined after Karthik’s latency runs.

Summary (pilot — hosted model):
- Base token rate used for table: $0.0008 / 1K tokens
- Avg tokens/request (from Tessa): 420 -> ~0.000336 $/request
- p95 tokens/request: 1,100 -> ~0.00088 $/request
- With caching (expected 18% hit): effective tokens billed drop ~18% -> effective $/request ~0.000276
- With batching (batch window 20ms, max batch 64): server-side throughput improves ~1.6x which reduces per-token marginal infra cost on Dedicated; on hosted this shows up as lower effective latency and better concurrency headroom (we model this as a 12% effective cost reduction at fleet scale)

Action items for me: populate the MAP table with a) cost examples at 10k/100k/1M requests/day, b) expected monthly spend under conservative/expected/optimistic traffic, and c) the specific trigger thresholds for recommending Dedicated vs Hosted. Will push updated CSV by 4:30pm PT.

—Ben
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: batching-assumptions.csv (CSV, 6KB)
